headline: The values we build by.
intro: Our values are not posters on a wall. They are decisions we make in every line of code, every contract, and every classroom.
aside: These are, technically, posters. Flip one over to see the decision behind it.

items.name: Dignity
items.statement: Every person affected by our technology deserves respect, privacy, and a voice. We never treat people as data points.
items.poster: No one is a data point.

practice.code: Personal data is minimized at the schema level. If a field is not needed to serve someone, it does not exist.
practice.contracts: Clients own their data outright. We claim no right to train on it, resell it, or keep it after the work ends.
practice.classroom: Every training starts with the people in the room, not the tools on the slide. Nobody is behind.

items.name: Justice
items.statement: We design against bias from the start and audit for it long after launch. Fairness is not a feature we add. It is a standard we meet.
items.poster: Fairness is a standard, not a feature.

practice.code: Ranking and recommendation logic is tested against outcomes for different groups before release, and re-tested on a schedule.
practice.contracts: Audit findings go to the client in writing, including the ones that make us look bad.
practice.classroom: We teach people to spot a biased output themselves, so the check never depends on us.

items.name: Transparency
items.statement: We explain how our systems work in plain language. If people cannot understand it, they cannot trust it, and they should not have to.
items.poster: If you can't understand it, you shouldn't have to trust it.

practice.code: When AI produced a result, the interface says so and shows the sources it used.
practice.contracts: Our data practices are written at an eighth grade reading level and attached to every agreement.
practice.classroom: If we cannot explain a tool simply, we do not recommend it.

items.name: Accountability
items.statement: We measure our success by real outcomes for real people, and we own what we build, including its mistakes.
items.poster: We own what we build. Mistakes included.

practice.code: Every release has a named owner and a changelog anyone can read.
practice.contracts: We define what "working" means with you before we start, and we report against it.
practice.classroom: Participants rate every session, and the numbers go to the whole team, not a drawer.

items.name: Community
items.statement: The people closest to the problem are closest to the solution. We build with communities, not for them or around them.

practice.code: Project Lookout was designed with BECMA members, tested inside their businesses, and reshaped by what they told us.
practice.contracts: Community partners are named collaborators, not "users," and they are credited.
practice.classroom: Cohorts are built from the same community, so the learning keeps going after we leave.

items.name: Shared Prosperity
items.statement: Every engagement should leave your team, your organization, and your neighborhood stronger than we found it.

practice.code: We favor tools an organization can run and afford on its own, including open source and local models, over subscriptions that lock it in.
practice.contracts: No minimum contract size. Pricing is scaled to the organization, not the other way around.
practice.classroom: Train-the-trainer programs, so the capacity stays inside the organization.
